reviews.rationale: The helper Base64-encodes SHA-256(code_verifier), removes padding, and maps the standard alphabet to the URL-safe alphabet before the challenge is sent in an OAuth authorization request. RFC 7636 requires the S256 code challenge to be BASE64URL(SHA256(ASCII(code_verifier))) and defines base64url without padding. The contract covers this output mapping only; it does not claim verifier entropy, state generation, server enforcement, or CSRF correctness.

review_refs.why: PKCE helper requires Web Crypto random values and computes S256 challenge
OAuth login submits the code challenge while retaining the verifier locally

reviews.rationale: binToUrlBase64 creates each DPoP JWS compact component from the JSON header/claims bytes and Web Crypto signature bytes. The transformation removes padding and maps the two standard Base64 symbols to the URL-safe alphabet before dot-joining the three components. RFC 7515 requires these protected-header, payload, and signature components to use unpadded Base64URL. The contract covers this output mapping only; it does not claim DPoP claim validity, key custody, or server acceptance.

review_refs.why: DPoP header and claims are encoded before creating the signing input
signature bytes are encoded and joined as the final DPoP compact component
exact Base64URL encoder used for both text and signature bytes

reviews.rationale: This helper percent-decodes encodeURIComponent output before Base64URL conversion, but its only caller passes JSON.stringify of an internally constructed DPoP header and claims object. The header contains fixed ASCII fields and exported JWK Base64URL strings; claims contain an integer timestamp and ASCII UUID. No non-ASCII text reaches this regex in the pinned call path, so a UTF-8 conversion proof here would be vacuous for the product flow.

review_refs.why: the DPoP header and claims fields are constructed from fixed strings, exported JWK values, integer timestamp, and UUID
the only callers JSON-stringify these constructed ASCII-only objects before strToUrlBase64
percent escape regex is in the private UTF-8 conversion helper
